episodes.207126: A nearby trough and the presence of a nearby stationary boundary led to thunderstorm development early in the morning of the 18th in West Texas. One storm managed to produce severe winds as it moved through Crane.
episodes.207158: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across northeastern Oklahoma during the late afternoon and evening of the 18th, along and just ahead of a cold front moving through the region. Weak instability ahead of the front, combined with moderately strong wind fields and wind shear associated with an upper level disturbance translating through the Southern Plains, resulted in the development of a supercell thunderstorm that produced large hail up to golf ball size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.207303: During the overnight/early morning hours of October 18th, storms brought damaging wind gusts to Leavenworth County, KS.
episodes.207304: During the overnight/early morning hours of October 18th, a storm brought damaging wind gusts to Clay County, MO.
episodes.207326: An upper level trough shifted east through the Central and Southern Plains during the afternoon/evening of October 18th, reinforcing a cold front southeast into Southwest Arkansas, Northeast Texas, and North Louisiana. A hot and humid air mass was present ahead of the front, with temperatures climbing into the mid 80s to near 90 degrees. When combined with ample low level moisture present, moderate instability was in place, with increasing wind shear ahead of the front/trough resulting in multi-cell thunderstorms developing during the afternoon and evening. Some of these storms became severe, with damaging winds downing trees and power lines across portions of extreme Eastern Texas, Southern Arkansas, and North Louisiana before the storms exited the region into the Lower Mississippi Valley after midnight.
episodes.207330: An upper level trough shifted east through the Central and Southern Plains during the afternoon/evening of October 18th, reinforcing a cold front southeast into Southwest Arkansas, Northeast Texas, and North Louisiana. A hot and humid air mass was present ahead of the front, with temperatures climbing into the mid 80s to near 90 degrees. When combined with ample low level moisture present, moderate instability was in place, with increasing wind shear ahead of the front/trough resulting in multi-cell thunderstorms developing during the afternoon and evening. Some of these storms became severe, with damaging winds downing trees and power lines across portions of extreme Eastern Texas, Southern Arkansas, and North Louisiana before the storms exited the region into the Lower Mississippi Valley after midnight. Unfortunately, one fatality was reported in Union Parish after lightning struck a deer stand, setting it on fire and killing a 17 year old male hunter inside.
episodes.207486: A storm system of mainly multi-cluster strong to severe storms moved across the Ozarks producing localized reports of quarter sized hail. Additionally, strong winds downed several trees and caused power outages with limbs and trees on powerlines. At least one structure was struck by lightning causing damage by fire.
episodes.207683: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northwest Indiana during the afternoon of October 18th producing isolated wind damage.
episodes.207751: The region was in the warm sector of deepening low pressure. Abundant shear, but somewhat limited instability resulted in the development of thunderstorms. While most remained below severe levels, one did produce marginally severe hail.
episodes.207787: An approaching cold front to the northwest of Arkansas in combination with temperatures which soared well into the 80s led to the development of isolated storms along an outflow boundary which led to a few isolated instances of severe weather across Arkansas.
episodes.207966: A line of thunderstorms developed out ahead of the cold. Due to weak instability, these storms were generally below severe limits, however, one isolated report of tree damage occurred in Effingham County.
episodes.207987: A brief period of scattered thunderstorms occurred during the afternoon of October 18, triggered by the season's first strong cold front. While most storms were non-severe, isolated instances of hail and wind damage were reported.
episodes.208132: An unstable weather pattern supported periods of enhanced shower and thunderstorm activity across Puerto Rico. Thunderstorms developed mainly during the afternoon, resulting in localized impacts, including flooding, hail, and lightning-related incidents.

This brief QLCS (Quasi-Linear Convective System) tornado started near Sycamore Drive in Hot Spring County, just north of Arkansas State Highway 128, and produced mainly tree damage along a short path. The tornado moved eastward, and dissipated as it reached Owasso Trail. Survey results found damage consistent with an EF1 tornado with winds of 105 mph.
